newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bardot's son, ex-husband seek cuts in memoirs.
newsitem.headline: Bardot's son, ex-husband seek cuts in memoirs.

text.p: The son and an ex-husband of French actress Brigitte Bardot took her to court on Wednesday seeking cuts from her memoirs branding her baby a "tumour" and her former spouse a "vulgar macho".
The Paris court said it would rule on October 31 over Jacques and Nicolas Charrier's request for 80 pages to be cut from Bardot's 555-page "Initiales B.B." under France's strict privacy laws.

The often embittered kiss-and-tell autobiography brands Jacques Charrier, an actor-turned-producer who was married to Bardot from 1959 to 1963, as "a vulgar, dictatorial and uncontrolled macho, a gigolo, alcoholic and despicable".

Bardot, 62, now an animal rights campaigner, recounts in detail how she felt suicidal when she learnt she was pregnant with her only son Nicolas, now 36. She calls the pregnancy a nightmare and the child a "tumour feeding off me".
She said at his birth: "I don't give a damn, I don't want to see him again." Bardot says later in the book she is now reconciled with Nicolas, who lives in Norway.

The Charriers' lawyer, Karen Berrebi, urged the court to excise a string of passages from future editions of the book both in France and abroad and to order publication of its ruling in six magazines.

Berrebi read out letters Bardot wrote to Jacques Charrier, second of her four husbands, during her pregnancy declaring her love for him. The lawyer said Bardot was a "liar" for denouncing him in her book about a life of glitz and solitude.
Before the court hearing, Bardot said she regretted the court battle. "I think this is a pity, it hurts me," she told Europe 1 radio.

Her lawyer, Wallerand de Saint-Just, argued: "The life of Brigitte Bardot and Jacques Charrier is part of the history of France, and one cannot ask for a ban on people writing about historical events."

Publishers of "Initiales B.B." say that the work has sold 395,000 copies since it came out less than a month ago, spiced by details of Bardot's turbulent sex life and by controversy over her sympathies with the far right of French politics.
